messages:
jamie: heads up — i'll be handing primary to @lee in ~10m. seeing a spike in p99 latency on text-generation for eu-west-1 (~1200ms -> 3400ms). Incident bot flagged 3xx and 5xx surge. leaving concise handoff + quick fixes below.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT 2026-03-15T03:12Z - multiple 3xx/5xx from /v1/generate, p99 latency >3000ms, pages sent to #eng-oncall.

lee: ack, i'll take primary at :10. any known customer-impact right now?

jamie: partial. A/B traffic routing shows ~8% of requests getting transient errors (mostly 503), overall success rate still ~92%. No major customer SLA pages yet but seeing uptick in retries from mobile clients. Creating brief runbook list below.

sanjay: quick checklist i recommend on takeover: 
- verify capacity: `rctl capacity describe --region eu-west-1`
- check kv-cache miss rate: metrics > Observability > kvcache/eu-west-1
- consider rolling model variant to low-memory quantized for latency-sensitive routes (fallback)

lee: on it. i'll run quick health probes and scale if needed.

ops-bot: NOTE: recent deploy to inference-worker in eu-west-1 at 02:58Z by ci-bot. No automatic rollback triggered.

jamie: key runbooks/links (short):
- primary mitigation play: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/fast-latency-mitigation (steps 1-4)
- kv-cache troubleshooting: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-stall
- model fallback guide: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-variants-fallback
- quick restart (k8s): https://redwood.internal/runbooks/k8s-restarts

immediate quick actions (do these first):
1) scale up inference-workers by +20% for eu-west-1: `rctl capacity adjust --region eu-west-1 --pct +20`
2) check workers with high mem: `kubectl top pods -n inference --selector=region=eu-west-1`
3) if worker pods repeatedly OOM or stuck in CrashLoopBackOff, restart pool: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-worker -n inference --namespace=prod`
4) enable hotspot fallback for route `/v1/generate`: toggle in console -> Routing -> Fallback -> enable minimal-quant model (applies instantly)

lee: running the scale now. starting health probes and tailing logs. `kubectl logs -f deploy/inference-worker -n prod --tail=200`

jamie: quick note on customer comms — @support-monitoring: flag customers with >5% error rate in last 15m. No widespread outage but call out those with sustained retries.

sanjay: also check KV cache miss spikes — if miss rate > 15% in last 10m, do a warm cache refresh for top prefixes: `scripts/warm_kv_cache --region eu-west-1 --routes /v1/generate`

lee: scaled +20% done. pod startup looks healthy, initial p99 dropped to ~1600ms (improvement). still seeing some 503s from two older worker nodes. investigating.

jamie: if those two nodes show older driver/kernel at boot, cordon and replace: `kubectl cordon <node>` then evict pods. link to node replacement doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/node-replacement

ops-bot: METRICS SNAPSHOT: p50 180ms, p95 520ms, p99 1700ms, error-rate 6.8% (5m window).

lee: found one worker with repeated `KVCacheTimeoutError` in logs — will drain and restart it.

sanjay: while you drain, toggle retry budget lower for mobile route to avoid client retries amplification: Console -> RateLimits -> mobile-client -> retry_budget=2

jamie: handoff notes for @lee taking primary:
- primary until 10:40Z, i'll be reachable via DM if needed.
- major actions already done: +20% scale, identified 2 problematic nodes, warm cache script queued, fallback model option available.
- watch p99 and error-rate for next 15m; escalate to infra if p99 > 2500ms after scale.

lee: taking primary now. i'll keep this thread updated. putting quick-running commands in thread for whoever follows: 
```
# check stuck pods
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running

# restart one pod safely
kubectl delete pod <pod-name> -n inference --grace-period=30 --wait

# run warm cache
scripts/warm_kv_cache --region eu-west-1 --routes /v1/generate --top 200
```

oncall-bot: REMINDER: please update the incident channel once stable and add owner for postmortem.

lee: will do. current plan: drain two nodes, restart one worker where KV errors spike, monitor for 10m. If errors persist, enable model fallback and open a capacity increase ticket.

jamie: for the handoff log — post-incident owner: @sanjay for root-cause & PM coordination, postmortem target within 72h.

lee: update 03:18Z — drained node-13, restarted worker pool on node-14. p99 now ~980ms, error-rate 1.6%. markers look good. keeping primary and will hand back at 03:40Z unless anything else pops.

sanjay: filing follow-up ticket with logs + prod link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-2026-0423 (assign @sanjay).

jamie: thanks team. final handoff checklist for whoever next takes over: 
- check p99/p95 in Observability;
- verify fallback model toggle is off if not needed;
- confirm node replacements scheduled and capacity commit updated if required;
- add a short note to the incident ticket about warm-cache step and the two affected nodes.

lee: handing back to @jamie at 03:40Z. leaving a short summary in the ticket and closing out the active page if all green. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (interim) at 03:40Z — p99 back within SLO and error-rate <2% for 10m.

jamie: closing thread. postmortem owner is @sanjay — please link runbooks used and any necessary updates. thanks all. :heart:
